author: Stevens
authority: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela, a member of the judgment coalition, assigns this lead opinion.
form: Form fixed before authorship or balance counts: one signed opinion of the Court after plenary merits submission. The municipal-liability rule and the limited Rule 56 application form one supported rationale; no separate lead or changed form is needed.
reason: Fit governs the already unanimous formulation. Stevens's Collins opinion directly separates the underlying constitutional deprivation from municipal attribution, which is the County's dispositive objection here. His Carter join supplies the demanding notice and causation limits needed to explain why this evidence permits proceedings without establishing liability. Ginsburg is the strongest alternative through her Carter opinion and can carry the same rule; Stevens has the lower count and is equally positioned to preserve the right/attribution distinction in this custody setting. Stone's full approved position agrees with that work, but his conditional future equitable proposal supplies no present drafting advantage. No commitment changes, accommodation or author-driven alteration of scope occurs.
